Top-K Relative Frequency Contrast Profile

Source: R/rfcp_top_k.R
rfcp_top_k.Rd

Discovers the top-K contrasting patterns (Platos) between a positive time series and a negative time series using an iterative Relative Frequency Contrast Profile (RFCP) procedure.

Usage

rfcp_top_k(
  positive_data,
  negative_data,
  window_size,
  k_platos = 2L,
  max_freq = 5L,
  exclusion_radius = NULL,
  min_rms = 1e-04,
  adaptive_max_freq = FALSE,
  min_freq = 2L,
  n_workers = 1L,
  backend = "cpu",
  progress = FALSE,
  query_block_size = NULL,
  progress_callback = NULL,
  checkpoint_callback = NULL,
  resume_state = NULL
)

Arguments

positive_data

Numeric positive/query time series.

negative_data

Numeric negative/reference time series.

window_size

Integer subsequence length, at least 2 and no larger than either input series.

k_platos

Integer number of distinct Platos to discover. Defaults to 2L.

max_freq

Integer scalar or integer vector specifying the number of non-overlapping neighbor ranks requested for each Plato iteration. If a scalar is provided, it is used for all iterations. If a vector is provided, its length must equal k_platos, allowing dynamic re-evaluation of frequency for rarer morphologies. Defaults to 5L.

exclusion_radius

Integer exclusion radius between accepted neighbor starts and for padding concatenated segments. NULL uses window_size.

min_rms

Numeric threshold for root-mean-square contrast. Iteration stops early if the detected Plato has an RMS contrast below this value. Defaults to 1e-4.

adaptive_max_freq

Logical. If TRUE, dynamically adapts max_freq for subsequent iterations based on the observed support (number of valid positive self-join neighbors with distance below \(\sqrt{2 \cdot \text{window\_size}}\)) of the current Plato. Defaults to FALSE.

min_freq

Integer minimum rank frequency floor when adaptive_max_freq = TRUE. Defaults to 2L.

n_workers

Number of native worker threads for the CPU backend. Ignored when backend = "cuda". Defaults to 1L.

backend

Computation backend: "cpu" (default) or "cuda".

progress

Logical progress flag for each RFCP iteration. Defaults to FALSE.

query_block_size

Optional integer query block size for chunked execution. If NULL (default), queries are processed monolithically in a single call. If specified, queries are processed in contiguous blocks of size query_block_size.

progress_callback

Optional callback function function(event) invoked periodically with structured progress events ("round_start", "block_done", "round_done").

checkpoint_callback

Optional callback function function(state) invoked after each block and Plato with a serializable state list.

resume_state

Optional state list from a previous execution (checkpoint_callback) used to resume execution idempotently.

Value

An object of class "rfcp_top_k", which is a list containing:

  • k_requested: requested number of Platos.

  • k_found: number of Platos discovered before stopping.

  • window_size: subsequence length.

  • exclusion_radius: exclusion radius used.

  • adaptive_max_freq: whether adaptive frequency was enabled.

  • min_freq: minimum frequency floor used.

  • max_freq: vector of frequencies used for each Plato.

  • platos: list of discovered Plato objects, each containing:

    • k: Plato iteration rank (1, 2, ...).

    • plato_index: one-based start index in positive_data.

    • plato_rms: contrast score at plato_index.

    • plato_subsequence: numeric vector containing the pattern.

    • plato_twin_index: one-based start index of nearest self-join neighbor.

    • rfcp_at_plato: clipped contrasts across accepted ranks.

    • rfmp_aa_at_plato: positive self-join distances.

    • rfmp_ab_at_plato: negative AB distances.

    • rfmpi_aa_at_plato: positive neighbor indices.

    • rfmpi_ab_at_plato: negative neighbor indices.

    • effective_max_freq: highest paired rank observed.

  • negative_data_final: the negative series augmented with the suppressed Plato occurrences and exclusion zones.

Details

In each iteration \(i \in \{1, \dots, K\}\), the algorithm:

  1. Executes rfcp using the current augmented negative series and the requested frequency max_freq[i].

  2. Identifies the highest-contrast query window (\(\text{Plato}_i\)) outside the exclusion zone of previously discovered Platos and their associated neighbors.

  3. If the contrast score is below min_rms or no valid candidate remains, iteration terminates early.

  4. Extracts the subsequences of \(\text{Plato}_i\) and all its accepted positive self-join neighbors (rfmpi_aa_at_plato), expanded by the exclusion zone: $$[\max(1, j - \text{exclusion\_radius}), \min(N^{(+)}, j + \text{window\_size} - 1 + \text{exclusion\_radius})]$$

  5. Merges overlapping intervals to maintain signal continuity, and appends the resulting segments to the negative series separated by NA barriers. Because rfcp is NA-aware, this suppresses the contrast of that morphology and its trivial overlaps in subsequent iterations without introducing spurious cross-boundary windows.

  6. If adaptive_max_freq = TRUE, re-evaluates the frequency for the next iteration based on the count of finite AA neighbors with distance below \(\sqrt{2 \cdot \text{window\_size}}\), bounded below by min_freq.

Examples

set.seed(42)
# Create positive series with 5 sine pulses and 2 cosine pulses
t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 20)
sine_pulse <- sin(t)
cos_pulse <- cos(t)
pos <- rnorm(300, sd = 0.05)
for (p in c(20, 60, 100, 140, 180)) pos[p:(p + 19)] <- pos[p:(p + 19)] + sine_pulse
for (p in c(220, 260)) pos[p:(p + 19)] <- pos[p:(p + 19)] + cos_pulse * 1.5
neg <- rnorm(300, sd = 0.05)

top_platos <- rfcp_top_k(pos, neg, window_size = 20, k_platos = 2, max_freq = c(4, 2))
print(top_platos)
#> Top-2 Relative Frequency Contrast Profile (RFCP)
#> Window size: 20 | Exclusion radius: 20 | Requested: 2 | Adaptive: FALSE
#>   Plato 1: index = 97, RMS = 0.683502, max_freq = 4 (twin = 177)
#>   Plato 2: index = 279, RMS = 0.341239, max_freq = 2 (twin = 239)
